turns.question: How can a lens in eyeglasses bend light, and how does that connect to this water lesson
turns.answer: A lens in eyeglasses bends light because light changes speed and direction when it passes through materials with different densities (like air to glass). This is similar to how light bends at the water surface, making a straight pencil appear bent. Light travels straight in one medium but refracts (bends) at angled boundaries. turns.answer: Bending in eyeglasses happens because light changes speed and direction as it passes through different materials, like from air into glass.
